added_models.model: Rat and monkey ketamine-challenge phMRI/EEG reversal

engagement.note: Takeda set reversal of ketamine-induced EEG gamma and BOLD changes in rats and monkeys as the readout a healthy-volunteer study must reproduce.
engagement.short: Animal ketamine readout set as gate
engagement.quote: The main objective was to demonstrate that the effects of TAK-063 were consistent in nonclinical and clinical studies, and the decision to move into phase 2 development was contingent on consistency between phase 1 results and critical preclinical data.
engagement.confidence_note: Proxy opening year: the Go-criteria table names the rat and monkey findings before the human study began (NCT01892189, start 2013-08); the animal data were published in Tomimatsu 2016 (doi 10.1016/j.neuroscience.2016.10.006, abstract read).
engagement.judgement: Opened at the start of the human ketamine study that the animal readout gated; the readout is downstream of PDE10A, unlike the draft's striatal cAMP/cGMP track.

engagement.note: TAK-063 reduced ketamine-induced resting BOLD effect sizes in key regions in 27 healthy men, as it had in rats and monkeys.
engagement.short: Ketamine BOLD reversal reproduced in humans
engagement.quote: Our results are consistent with non-clinical studies of ketamine and TAK-063 and clinical studies of ketamine and risperidone.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract read; effect sizes rather than significance tests are reported. Registry results for NCT01892189 were posted 2017-01-12 but do not state the comparison.
engagement.reason: Human ketamine BOLD moved as in animals
engagement.judgement: Stated comparison dated to the paper's online date (2019-11-26); a pairing of Tomimatsu 2016 with the 2017 registry posting could date it to 2017. Healthy volunteers count for engagement.
engagement.magnitude_basis: Reduction of ketamine-induced resting-state BOLD effect size (Cohen's d)

efficacy.note: Takeda ran a ketamine challenge in healthy men to test whether TAK-063 blocks ketamine-induced brain changes and psychotic-like symptoms before phase 2.
efficacy.quote: Effects of TAK-063 on Preventing Ketamine-Induced Brain Activity Changes as Well as Psychotic-Like Symptoms in Healthy Male Adults
efficacy.confidence_note: Registry record: first posted 2013-07-04, start 2013-08, completed 2014-08.
efficacy.judgement: Quote is the registry title; the study was run before any member's patient efficacy result, so it is a prospective model, not a retrodiction.

efficacy.note: The ketamine challenge met Takeda's Go criterion, but TAK-063 20 mg missed the PANSS primary endpoint in acute schizophrenia (p=0.115).
efficacy.quote: The primary endpoint, change from baseline in the Positive and Negative Syndrome Scale total score at week 6, was not achieved (least-squares mean difference vs placebo [standard error] = -5.46 [3.44]; p = 0.115).
efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level reading. Model side: Takeda 2020 full text (PMC7689203) records the Go decision but does not mention the phase 2 result, so this is a pairing; Yurgelun-Todd 2020 itself says predictivity was unknown.
efficacy.reason: Human challenge passed; patient trial failed
efficacy.judgement: Paired, not stated. Dated to the NCT02477020 results posting (2017-09-29); the challenge's own results were posted 2017-01-12. Takeda states the phase 1 results 'showed some consistent evidence of antipsychotic activity', so the model predicted benefit. Magnitude null: the drug was numerically better but not separated.
efficacy.magnitude_basis: PANSS total change vs placebo at week 6

considered_not_added: PDE10A loss-of-function genetics (Diggle 2016 biallelic, Mencacci 2016 de novo GAF-B): no source draws a prediction for inhibitor side effects or efficacy; Mencacci points the other way (modulation could treat chorea); Diggle full text not retrievable. A pairing with member dystonia would be my own inference.

MK-8189 rat CAR/PPI occupancy-efficacy model guiding clinical dose (Smith 2025 JPET): same system as the draft's rodent exposure/occupancy dose track; the phase 2b at doses predicted to give up to 80% occupancy failed (2026), which reinforces the existing dose contra.
MK-8189 rhesus ketamine object-retrieval cognition model: no patient cognition comparison found; member trials used PANSS.
TAK-063 cognition batteries and EEG gamma in stable patients (MRD study NCT01879722): 'data not shown' in Takeda 2020 and not a primary-endpoint comparison.
Rhesus/human PDE10A PET occupancy translation ([11C]T-773, [11C]MK-8193): already the draft's engagement track (Takano 2016).
Lu AF11167 negative-symptom rationale: no published preclinical model found; its trial (Meyer-Lindenberg 2022, doi 10.1016/j.euroneuro.2022.05.009) failed on BNSS but has no model side to pair.
OMS824 rat high-dose toxicology finding (Omeros 2015): stopped trials, no patient comparison.
QSP / computer-modeling of PDE10A inhibitors (Geerts/In Silico Biosciences): only reviews found (Geerts 2017, 2019), no dated PDE10A prediction to compare.
Primate EPS/dyskinesia models for members: none found.
Patient-derived cells, organoids or ex-vivo assays: none for this class in schizophrenia.

gaps.lead: DeMartinis et al. 2012 SIRS Poster #212 (doi 10.1016/s0920-9964(12)70783-1), PF-02545920 monotherapy phase 2a
gaps.detail: Corrects the date of efficacy index 2 (rodent-antipsychotic-screens, contra) from 2016 to 2012; the checker verdict on efficacy index 2 already proposes 2012. Any earlier dating of dose index 2 (pde10a-rodent-exposure-occupancy) needs a verdict once the poster text is read.

gaps.lead: OMS824 (member): Omeros suspended PDE10 trials in 2015 after a rat high-dose toxicology finding
gaps.detail: A preclinical finding that stopped trials, with no patient result to compare, falls outside the rule that a system must be compared with patient results. Already listed in considered_not_added.

gaps.lead: Lu AF11167 NCT03793712 (stopped for futility), registry_date null
gaps.detail: A date field on efficacy index 2 (rodent-antipsychotic-screens), patient_trials row NCT03793712. No results are posted; the earliest public date is Meyer-Lindenberg 2022 (doi 10.1016/j.euroneuro.2022.05.009). The status stays contra, so no new system is needed.

gaps.lead: Roche RG7203 reward-processing fMRI/MID model in healthy volunteers, then chronic schizophrenia patients (Schizophr Bull 2018 suppl S43)
gaps.detail: RG7203 is a Roche PDE10A inhibitor and not one of the tile's five members (Lu AF11167, OMS824, balipodect, elpipodect, mardepodect), so a non-member drug falls outside the rules.
